analysis.title: Silver Futures: Surviving the Hot CPI
key_insights: A month of selling into the US midterm elections left speculative silver positioning near a multiyear minimum. Non-Dealers sold every week from Oct 6 to Nov 3 for a cumulative $2.3bn, per Commitment of Traders data.
New shorts of $2.6bn were partly offset by new longs of $300mm. Managed Money sold $1.4bn and Non-Reportable sold $1.4bn, while the Other category bought $470mm.
Net length in notional terms was at the 2nd percentile on a 2-year lookback (reported as '2%').
Silver rose about 6% from Nov 3 to Nov 9 after the election outcome lifted China Solar stocks and lowered the Dollar. GS says the Democratic sweep implied more favorable trade policy.
GS's China Solar basket rose 7.1% in the same window, while Data Center stocks fell. GS calls Data Center stocks a less important structural demand indicator for silver.
Over the past 6 months, changes in Managed Money gross longs have been positively correlated with China Solar. GS reads this as a sign that long buying potentially returned in at least one cohort.
Silver's 3-month normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened from its highest level since Covid, which GS reads as a retracement from peak fear in the option surface.
Silver fell 2.8% on Nov 10 on the hot CPI report, then rebounded about 3% in early trading on Nov 11.

macro_indicators.reading: Described as a hot report. No figure is given.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Silver fell 2.8% on Nov 10 after the CPI report and recovered about 3% in early Nov 11 trading. GS says silver has survived the report.

risk_factors: Hot CPI prints can hit silver, as the 2.8% drop on Nov 10 showed.
Positioning is thin, so the Nov 3 to 9 rally may rest on a small group of buyers. GS only says long buying 'potentially' returned.
